subject: Scheduling: Deep-dive demo & SE call - timezone coordination
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@acme-eu.com>; Kenji Sato <kenji.sato@platformjp.co.jp>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-01T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Scheduling: Deep-dive demo & SE call - timezone coordination

Hi Laura / Kenji —

Thanks again for the interest in Redwood. As discussed, we'd like to schedule a technical deep-dive with one of our solutions engineers to walk through the architecture, network requirements, and a live demo tailored to your architects. I copied Logan (SE) and Priyom (Solutions Lead).

Given your team spans EU and APAC, can you share a few 1–2 hour windows that work for your architects in the next two weeks? To help, here's what we can offer from our side: 
- Logan is available Mon/Wed/Fri mornings PT (US West) and Tue/Thu late afternoons PT.
- Priyom can support early Europe hours (CET) on Tue/Thu.

If you prefer, we can propose specific overlap windows — happy to handle the calendar invite. Also, note that the US shifts to DST on 2026-03-08 which may affect availability if we go later in March.

Example overlap windows (all shown in local zones for clarity):
- 08:00 PT / 16:00 CET / 00:00 JST (next day) — okay for senior architects who can take a late EU / overnight APAC slot.
- 11:00 PT / 19:00 CET / 03:00 JST (next day) — less ideal for APAC.
- 20:00 PT / 04:00 CET (next day) / 12:00 JST — works for APAC daytime but late for US.

Please let us know 2–3 preferred windows and any constraints (e.g., no calls before 09:30 CET; Kenji prefers Japan daytime). Once we settle on a time, I'll send a calendar invite with an .ics and the network checklist.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0138

--

Hi Marissa —

Thanks — that framing is helpful. Our core architects are based in Berlin (CET) and Tokyo (JST). Kenji is flexible but prefers Japan business hours if possible. A few constraints from our side: 
- EU architects unavailable before 09:30 CET.
- We prefer not to have meetings after 19:30 CET.
- Week of 2026-03-15 we have a release freeze, so earlier in March is better.

Suggested pockets that might work for us (all local times):
- Tue 2026-03-03: 16:00–18:00 CET (would be 00:00–02:00 JST — Kenji can do up to 01:30 JST)
- Wed 2026-03-04: 09:30–11:30 CET (would be 17:30–19:30 JST) — US West would be overnight.
- Thu 2026-03-05: 18:00–20:00 CET (02:00–04:00 JST) — only if we absolutely need overlap with US late evening windows.

If you can propose exact slots in CET/JST with the corresponding PT times, that would be great. We can loop in procurement separately for contract/terms.

Best,
Laura
Laura Chen
Head of Cloud Architecture, Acme Corp
laura.chen@acme-eu.com

Hi Laura —

Thanks for the constraints, that's helpful. A few quick notes on logistics and DST: 
- The US moves to DST on 2026-03-08 which shifts PT from UTC-8 to UTC-7; since you're asking for early March slots we're currently still on standard time in the US.
- When converting across PT/CET/JST it's easiest to pick a single proposal window and offer a 1.5–2 hour block. I recommend avoiding slots that land between 00:00–06:30 local time for any participant.

Proposed concrete windows (converted to all three zones) — all in 2026-03-03 / 03-04 timeframe: 
- Option A: Wed 2026-03-04 09:30–11:00 CET / Wed 2026-03-04 17:30–19:00 JST / Wed 2026-03-04 00:30–02:00 PT (late US night) — Logan can join remotely, Priyom may need to attend early EU slot.
- Option B: Tue 2026-03-03 16:00–17:30 CET / Wed 2026-03-04 00:00–01:30 JST / Tue 2026-03-03 07:00–08:30 PT — gives a morning PT window that works for some US participants and late JP overnight.
- Option C: Tue 2026-03-03 20:00–21:30 CET / Wed 2026-03-04 04:00–05:30 JST / Tue 2026-03-03 11:00–12:30 PT — this is US-friendly midday but will be late for EU.

If the customer's architects can confirm which of these options they prefer, we'll lock in the time and I will prepare the demo plan (network checklist, prep questions, sample prompts). If none are acceptable, we can propose shifting to March 5–6 or offer two shorter sessions for separate regions.

Cheers,
Logan Wright
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
logan_wright@redwood.ai

Hi Marissa / Logan —

Thanks for the options. Option A puts the demo at 17:30–19:00 JST which is fine for me and our Tokyo architects (we can make up to 19:30 JST). Option B would be tough because it starts at midnight local time. Option C is okay but means our EU team is late.

So we prefer Option A: Wed 2026-03-04 09:30–11:00 CET / 17:30–19:00 JST / 00:30–02:00 PT. If Priyom or Logan need a slightly earlier US start, we could do 23:30–01:00 PT (i.e., 08:30–10:00 CET).

Please send the invite and include the network checklist — our infra team will need the firewall rules and port list. Also add Kenji and me to the calendar and include the link to any recording.

Regards,
Kenji
